answer: Registration requires a domain delegated to the applicant. The agent publishes a TXT record carrying the epoch seed and its address, and three independent resolvers check that the record postdates the seed. One root domain backs one identity, so a thousand names cannot share a zone file. At about $11 a domain yearly, 1,000 clones pay $11,000 plus 1,000 nameservers answering each new seed within six hours, work no registrar lets one account script. Picture a terrace on a dune: one shared wall, yet every door needs its own copper pair back to the exchange, billed per pair.
